neighbours.label: the word-final subword piece 'ana' or 'ina' (Tijuana, Fontana, Lucina, Catalina)
fire: Last spring we drove south and spent a weekend in Tijuana with friends.
The old fountain was designed by the architect Domenico Fontana.
My grandmother's name was Lucina, and she ran the village bakery.
From the harbour you can take the ferry to Santa Catalina Island.
The princess in that game, Rosalina, lives among the stars.
We caught the night train from Palermo to Messina.
A green iguana was sunning itself on the wall of the hotel.
Next summer they plan to visit Ljubljana and the lakes nearby.
quiet: Last spring we drove south and spent a weekend in Indiana with friends.
The old fountain was designed by the architect named Christina.
My grandmother's name was Regina, and she ran the village bakery.
From the harbour you can take the ferry to Marina Island.
The princess in that game, Tatiana, lives among the stars.
We caught the night train from Bologna to Ravenna.
A cocktail called a margarita was waiting on the table of the hotel.
Next summer they plan to visit Cartagena and the beaches nearby.

notes: Card: 'anus', 'ina', 'ana' x3, 'N' in names; probe: bandana/banana 0.53, Spadina 0.48, pandanus 1.1. Tokenizer checked: fire words split off 'ana'/'ina'; near misses are names that are one token or end in a different piece ('enna', 'ena', 'iana', 'ita').
